title: Honest Absolute Calibration of Treatment-Benefit Scores under Rough Selection and Baseline Risk
banked_reason: Sound bracket-plus-null-length result does not deliver the promised six-coordinate sharp frontier; four global logarithms remain open; projected paper-score ceiling 6.1 below field floor 7.4. Independent validity gate confirms no concrete bounded repair.
gap_reasons: The proposal's six-coordinate sharp Stat frontier is not delivered: this node explicitly leaves all four global risk/parent-honest-length logarithms, their exact risk-to-length orders, and sharp attaining procedures open, so the current kernel is a weaker bracket-plus-null-length result.

The exact calibrated-family length theorem is a genuine delivered result, but its theorem-level novelty is not positioned against the closest accepted-bank donors and closest same-criterion literature with a precise statement of what their targets, parent-honesty scope, and rates do not cover.
D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.1 < 7.4, so the graded tier field is capped at incremental.
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted the six sharp global-risk, full-parent honest-length, and calibrated-family criteria in observational and supplied-randomization experiments. Informal derivations matched calibrated-family lengths at n^(-4/13) and n^(-2/5), while all four global logarithmic orders and sharp simultaneous attainment remained open. Math review passed, but the six-object kernel was not delivered and the 6.1 package-score ceiling missed the field floor; no Lean formalization was attempted.
tldr: Absolute calibration of a supplied treatment-benefit score is an irregular scalar validation problem when the treatment contrast is smooth but treatment selection and baseline risk are rough. The benchmark fixes a public uniform covariate law, binary outcomes, H\"older exponent \(1/8\) for the unknown propensity and baseline, and a Lipschitz calibration residual with unrestricted zeros. The research target is the six-object matched frontier for absolute risk, finite-sample parent-honest connected-interval length, and expected length at perfect calibration, in both observational and supplied-assignment experiments. The novel proof boundary is the combination of original-record nuisance-product moment correction, uniform-envelope absolute-value approximation, and normalized correlated-nuisance mixtures. The exact logarithms, equality of risk and length orders, and optimal simultaneous length adaptation are outputs of the open questions.
gap: Existing treatment-effect calibration assessment, positive-gap irregular regression inference, and Gaussian nonsmooth norm theory leave the fixed original-record parent-honesty problem unresolved. Neither null testing alone nor a scalar plug-in estimate determines its matched length frontier.
fill: Integrated dyadic moment correction and lawful shared-nuisance mixture comparisons target explicit finite-sample rates and computationally finite honest intervals. Completion requires all six criteria and their supplied-assignment comparison; the elementary brackets are supporting content.
